title: Correct or remove program_ref_resolver.dart's false production-integration doc claims
rule: Evans (ubiquitous language / doc-reality drift) + Fowler (speculative generality)

evidence.quote:
/// calendar service. Production wires this to the local calendar engine
/// (DNI-330).

/// Dashboard, scheduler, and reader all consume this same resolver so they
/// agree on which `ContentItem` a calendar entry points to (FR16).

why: Two present-tense claims in this class's doc comment don't match the codebase. (1) 'Production wires this to the local calendar engine (DNI-330)' — docs/planning/epics.md:782 records DNI-330 as Story 25.9, 'core/labels/ rebuild — three new modes, ContentIndex consumer, static API deleted', unrelated to calendar-engine wiring. (2) 'Dashboard, scheduler, and reader all consume this same resolver' — scheduler_providers.dart:108 calls index.lookup() directly, bypassing ProgramRefResolver's whitespace/transliteration normalization entirely. Repo-wide grep for ProgramRefResolver(/ProgramRefSource confirms zero call sites outside this file and one story-acceptance test — the class is fully built, fully unit-tested, and has never been wired into any consumer. Whether the ad-hoc direct lookups in scheduler/dashboard/reader ever actually disagree (a live FR16 violation) is unverified — the calendar rows may be pre-canonicalized at seed time, which would make runtime resolution unnecessary in practice; that needs runtime/data confirmation, not just this static read.
recommendation: Either wire the named consumers (starting with scheduler_providers.dart:108) through ProgramRefResolver.resolve() so the FR16 claim is true, or rewrite the doc comment to state plainly that it isn't wired yet and cite the real tracking ticket (not DNI-330).
acceptance_criteria: program_ref_resolver.dart's doc comment cites an accurate ticket for production wiring, or states it is not yet wired.
If FR16 sharing is the intended design, at least scheduler_providers.dart's calendar-derived ref lookups route through ProgramRefResolver instead of a raw index.lookup().
